summary: No hallucinated files, functions or literals in any of the four tasks. Every named symbol, line-anchored literal, tech-debt item, docker invocation and infrastructure claim was checked against the tree; the four claims singled out for scrutiny all hold, including task 08's central 'reordering SQL aliases cannot redden a golden' argument. One acceptance criterion (task 08, mutation A5) rests on a mechanism the code does not have and cannot fire; the rest of the findings are vacuous-assertion notes and line-number drift.

Cross-task: internal/query/archiver.go does not exist yet, correctly declared as Task 01's wave-1 output and read-only in tasks 07/08/10; SelectStatArchiverQuery(_ int) (string, int, [2]int) returning DiffIntvl is fixed by task 01 and consumed by Configure per task 05, which is what makes mutation A1 valid.

findings.issue: Acceptance criterion A5 ('remove the archiver entry from view.New(): Test_app_doReport_Archiver turns red on all three subcases') rests on a mechanism the report path does not have. processData builds its own map - `views := view.Views{config.ReportType: v}` (report/report.go:282-284) - and Views.Configure switches on the MAP KEY, not on the registry (internal/view/view.go:372-373). With Task 05's `case "archiver":` present, a zero-value View under key "archiver" still receives QueryTmpl/Ncols/DiffIntvl from SelectStatArchiverQuery. The only view fields the report path then consumes are DiffIntvl/OrderKey/OrderDesc/UniqueKey (countDiff, report.go:505) plus Cols/ColsWidth computed by formatStatSample from the fixture; on a single-row archiver result OrderKey/OrderDesc/UniqueKey are inert (PGresult.sort returns without reordering one row). The output is therefore byte-identical with and without the view.New() entry, so the populated and never_archived goldens stay green - and the no_archiver_entries subcase, which asserts an empty buffer, cannot redden under any view change at all. The task's own rule ('when a mutation does not turn a test red ... Fix the test, then re-run') would send the executor chasing a red that replay cannot produce.
findings.fix: Drop A5, or restate it as what it actually guards: the registration is pinned by Task 05's own unit tests (internal/view/view_test.go TestNew / the Configure map test) and by record/record_test.go Test_filterViews, not by a replay golden. If a guard is wanted in this file, make it explicit - e.g. assert in the archiver test that view.New() contains an "archiver" entry with DiffIntvl{0,0} before driving doReport - and label it as a registry assertion rather than a golden mutation.

findings.issue: The empty-archive subcase's 'asserts doReport returns nil' is vacuous: doReport returns nil unconditionally (report/report.go:148-149) and reports processData errors with fmt.Println to stdout, never to app.writer. So both halves of that assertion (nil error, empty buffer) also hold when the pipeline failed - e.g. when isFilenameOK/isFilenameTimestampOK silently skipped every entry, which is the exact trap the task documents elsewhere in Edge cases.
findings.fix: Keep the assertions but state in the doc comment that only the buffer-empty half carries signal, and defend against the degenerate case by reusing an identical tar construction (same filename format and TsStart/TsEnd) as the populated subcase, so a filename/interval mistake reddens the populated golden first.

findings.issue: 'Also asserts the output contains no `n/a`' (never_archived subcase) cannot fail. `n/a` is a TUI sentinel - naLiteral = "n/a" at top/stat.go:430 - and the report package never emits it; blank cells are produced by %-*s padding in printStatSample (report/report.go:634). This is the same vacuity the task correctly rejects for the delta-`3` sentinel.
findings.fix: Drop the n/a assertion or replace it with something the report path could actually print if the blank handling regressed - the field-count assertion already covers `0`, `-` and `n/a` in one check; assert additionally that the data line does not contain the literal '-' as a standalone field.

findings.issue: Two internal/source inconsistencies. (a) The Description calls report/testdata/pgcenter.stat.golden.tar 'a 2021 PG14beta1 recording' while Verification Step 7 calls it 'the legacy PG13-era tar' - the fixture's sample timestamps are 2021-06-14 (report/report_test.go:59-77), i.e. the PG14 beta era, so the Description wording is the right one. (b) Line refs into report_record_statio_test.go drift: the single-golden precedent Test_app_doReport_StatIOTime starts at :185 (doc comment :176-184), not :177-206, and statIOStripANSI/statIOAnsiRE are at :42-47, not :43-46. The bgwriter refs are accurate.
findings.fix: Say 'the legacy 2021 PG14-beta fixture' in both places; refresh the two statio line anchors (or drop the line numbers and name the symbols, which do not drift).

findings.issue: The 'do not quote 0 B' hint names the wrong renderer for the backlog cell. The verbose row formats it through pretty.SizeWidth(float64(o.ArchivingBacklog), sizeFieldWidth) (top/stat.go:722-725), not pretty.Size directly - SizeWidth right-aligns Size(v) into a fixed-width field, so the rendered cell is a space-padded '0', not a bare '0'. The conclusion the hint draws is correct ('0 B' is not a screen literal, prose is the right form); only the attribution is off, and quoting a bare `0` as a screen literal would be almost as wrong as quoting `0 B`.
findings.fix: Amend the hint: 'the panel formats sizes through pretty.SizeWidth, which right-aligns pretty.Size(v) into a fixed-width field; pretty.Size returns "0" for zero (internal/pretty/pretty.go:11-12), so the cell shows a padded 0 and neither `0 B` nor a bare `0` should be quoted as a screen literal.'

findings.issue: depends_on lists only ["05"], but the task reads internal/query/archiver.go (Task 01, wave 1) as its source of truth for column names, documents Task 02's fpi,KiB column, and its acceptance criterion `pgcenter report -d -W a` requires Task 04's string -W flag. Task 05 declares depends_on ["01","02"], so 01 and 02 are transitively covered; Task 04 is not in that closure and is covered only by wave ordering (04 is wave 1, 07 is wave 3). The task text is explicit and honest about all three, so this is a declaration gap rather than an execution hazard.
findings.fix: Add "04" to depends_on (or keep as-is and note in the frontmatter comment that wave ordering covers it) so a re-planned wave assignment cannot silently break the -d -W a smoke check.

findings.issue: The verified docker invocation sets GOPATH=/gopath (empty inside the container) while the host module cache is mounted at /gomod only to supply GOROOT - so the run re-downloads all modules into the container and needs network access. This is the project's documented, previously-executed recipe (verified green on feature 016), not a defect, but a QA agent hitting a module download failure on an offline runner could misread it as a broken image or a dependency problem.
findings.fix: Add one line to Details: 'the container downloads modules into /gopath, so the run needs network; a download failure is an environment issue, not a suite failure'. Optionally mount the cache a second time as GOMODCACHE=/gomod/... to make the run hermetic.

findings.issue: The recorded stand pgpro@10.128.31.96 carries a 24h TTL from 2026-08-05 and is already past it as of today, so the manual half of this gate is blocked on a new address from the moment the task starts. The task handles this correctly (re-confirm first, NOT VERIFIABLE rather than PASS, never skip silently) - flagged only so the orchestrator requests a stand before scheduling wave 4 rather than mid-run.
findings.fix: No change to the task. Request the stand address at the start of wave 4; if none can be had, expect the archiving, navigation, narrow-terminal, subtitle and cost criteria to come back NOT VERIFIABLE and the verdict to be NEEDS WORK on evidence, not on defects.
